nodes.label: Every Output Is an Edit Surface
nodes.author: Jake Van Clief, David McDermott
nodes.rationale: Each stage's intermediate output is a file a human can open, edit and save before the next stage runs — implementing Horvitz's mixed-initiative principles and Shneiderman's direct manipulation paradigm. The pipeline is inherently interpretable because nothing was hidden.
nodes.norm_label: every output is an edit surface

nodes.label: Configure the Factory, Not the Product
nodes.author: Jake Van Clief, David McDermott
nodes.rationale: A workspace is set up once with preferences, brand and structure; each run then produces a new deliverable from the same configuration, following the continuous-delivery principle that pipelines should be repeatable.
nodes.norm_label: configure the factory, not the product

nodes.label: Five-Layer Context Hierarchy
nodes.author: Jake Van Clief, David McDermott
nodes.rationale: Layers 0-2 are structural routing (~800, ~300, 200-500 tokens); Layers 3-4 are content. No agent reads everything, which keeps token cost low and avoids the long-context degradation Liu et al. documented.

nodes.label: Interpretable Context Methodology (ICM)
nodes.author: Jake Van Clief, David McDermott
nodes.rationale: Replaces framework-level orchestration with filesystem structure: for sequential workflows with human review at each step, a coordination framework solves a problem that need not exist. Numbered folders are stages, markdown files carry the prompts, local scripts do the non-AI work. Open source under MIT.

nodes.label: Layer 3 — Reference Material (the factory)
nodes.author: Jake Van Clief, David McDermott
nodes.rationale: Stable across runs and configured once at workspace setup; the model should internalize it as constraints rather than process it as input. The recipe, not the ingredients.

nodes.label: Layer 4 — Working Artifacts (the product)
nodes.author: Jake Van Clief, David McDermott
nodes.rationale: Per-run output/ content that changes every execution; separating it from Layer 3 in the folder structure means the model receives already-organized context instead of sorting persistent rules from run artifacts itself.

nodes.label: Layered Context Loading
nodes.author: Jake Van Clief, David McDermott
nodes.rationale: Stage-specific loading is prevention rather than compression: rather than compressing an overstuffed context (Jiang et al.), never load the irrelevant material in the first place.

nodes.label: One Stage, One Job
nodes.author: Jake Van Clief, David McDermott
nodes.rationale: From McIlroy's Unix principle and Parnas's information-hiding criterion: a stage that fetches data does not also filter it. Each stage reads a defined input, transforms it, writes a defined output — the same structure as a pass in a multi-pass compiler.

nodes.label: Plain Text as the Interface
nodes.author: Jake Van Clief, David McDermott
nodes.rationale: Markdown and JSON only — no binary formats, no database connections, no proprietary serialization — so any tool that reads text and any human with an editor can inspect or modify any artifact (Kernighan and Pike).

nodes.label: Stage Contract Inputs Table (Layer 2 control point)
nodes.author: Jake Van Clief, David McDermott
nodes.rationale: Without an explicit Inputs table the agent would either load the whole workspace or rely on its own judgment; the table makes the selection explicit, editable and auditable — the filesystem doing the work a framework would otherwise do in code.
nodes.norm_label: stage contract inputs table (layer 2 control point)

nodes.label: Review Gate Protocol
nodes.author: Major Dream Williams
nodes.rationale: Read the stage summary, run the stage's verify checklist, then say 'Approved. Proceed to Stage N+1.' Never let Claude Code auto-proceed — this is the ICM architecture working as designed.

nodes.label: Build Phase Map (Phases 1-4)
nodes.author: Major Dream Williams
nodes.rationale: Stages 06 and 07 are explicitly blocked until Phase 1 ships to a real practitioner (Flo), so operator tooling and Stripe are never built ahead of demonstrated use.

nodes.label: Vercel Deployment and Env Var Split
nodes.author: Major Dream Williams
nodes.rationale: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY and VITE_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY must be used only inside the serverless function, never client-side; every push to main auto-deploys and branch pushes give preview URLs for reviewing stage output before merge.
nodes.norm_label: vercel deployment and env var split

nodes.label: Five-Layer Context Hierarchy (as applied to STB)
nodes.author: Major Dream Williams
nodes.rationale: Layer 0 CLAUDE.md 'where am I', Layer 1 CONTEXT.md 'where do I go', Layer 2 stage CONTEXT.md 'what do I do', Layer 3 _config stable reference, Layer 4 stage output working artifacts — one agent reading the right files at the right stage replaces a multi-agent framework.
nodes.norm_label: five-layer context hierarchy (as applied to stb)

nodes.label: STB Command Center
nodes.source_location: Layer 0 identity — What This Repo Is
nodes.author: Major Dream Williams
nodes.rationale: Built as a two-sided PWA rather than a web dashboard because practitioners open it on a phone at 7am; the stabilization layer sits before the full BWYH ascension path so the two stay connected but distinct.

nodes.label: Magic Link Auth Flow
nodes.rationale: No password at all, 30-day sessions — friction at the door contradicts the calm-room promise.

nodes.label: Row Level Security Policies
nodes.rationale: auth.uid() = practitioner_id on every table, operator tier reads all, no anonymous reads — the tier model is enforced in the database, not only in the UI gate.

nodes.label: AI Prompt (paid) — Claude suggests today's focus
nodes.norm_label: ai prompt (paid) — claude suggests today's focus

nodes.label: Typography Scale (Cormorant Garamond + DM Sans)
nodes.rationale: Font weight is capped at 500 because heavier weights 'read as wrong' against the serif display face and break the calm register.

nodes.label: PWA Manifest
nodes.rationale: start_url is /today, not /, so an installed icon opens straight into the morning room.

nodes.label: Stability Seeker Archetype
nodes.rationale: The overwhelmed gifted practitioner who reads a good client call as proof the business works and a quiet week as proof it does not — 'emotional weather', not data.

nodes.label: Practitioner View
nodes.rationale: Kept deliberately calm and minimal — one room, one focus, one action — because the target user is an overwhelmed practitioner, not a power user.

nodes.label: calculate_momentum_score (Postgres function)
nodes.rationale: Lives in Postgres rather than the client so the score cannot be manipulated from the browser; must return 0 for the zero-log edge case.

nodes.label: EvidenceScreen
nodes.rationale: 'Did it' and 'Didn't' are presented inline with equal weight and no modal, because both are valid data points under Evidence Over Vibes.

nodes.label: Trip Wire Button ("Something hit a wall")
nodes.rationale: Passes {task_name, leak_zone, practitioner_id} to the Stage 05 detector; the escape hatch is a first-class button so resistance gets routed instead of silently ending the streak.
nodes.norm_label: trip wire button ("something hit a wall")

nodes.label: Momentum Score (0-100)
nodes.rationale: Computed, never felt and never manually adjustable: last 7 days weighted 70%, prior 7 days 30%, plus +2 per consecutive day capped at +20 — a practitioner can only move it by logging.

nodes.label: Tier Architecture (Free / Paid / Operator)
nodes.rationale: AI features sit behind the paid tier so the free tier still delivers the daily habit loop (Today + Evidence) without cost per call.

nodes.label: ai_suggestions table
nodes.rationale: confirmed defaults false so Claude can never auto-confirm; every suggestion is persisted before display, leaving an audit trail of what the model proposed versus what a human accepted.

nodes.label: evidence_logs table
nodes.rationale: did_it is boolean and non-nullable, and momentum_score is computed and stored on write so the score is a historical fact rather than a recalculated view.

nodes.label: Feature 4 — Check-In Draft (operator only)
nodes.rationale: Drafted in Major Dream's brand voice and gated to tier === 'operator'; the operator edits and sends, so the message is always human-signed.

nodes.label: Feature 2 — Evidence Pattern Insight
nodes.rationale: Requires 14+ days of logs and must surface one specific non-obvious pattern with a systemic suggestion, never a motivational nudge.

nodes.label: Feature 1 — Today Focus Suggestion
nodes.rationale: Capped at 15 words with no motivational filler, and only fires when one_focus is empty, so the model fills a blank rather than overriding a human decision.

nodes.label: Feature 3 — Trip Wire Detector
nodes.rationale: Loads TRIP-WIRE-SYSTEM.md in full rather than a summary; the operator receives the typed diagnosis while the practitioner only ever sees a calm human message, never the label.

nodes.label: Human Oversight and Interpretability
nodes.rationale: Parasuraman and Riley's misuse/disuse failure modes both stem from the human not seeing what happened between input and output; Rudin argues for inherently interpretable systems over post-hoc explanation, and the EU AI Act now requires human oversight of high-risk systems.

nodes.label: Banned Words List
nodes.rationale: 'Submit', 'successfully', 'simply', 'dashboard', 'data' and the literal word 'AI' are banned: 'simply' condescends, 'data' distances the practitioner from their own proof, and 'AI' is replaced with 'Claude' so the suggestion reads as a named collaborator.

nodes.label: Empty State Structure
nodes.rationale: Each empty state says what it is, why it is empty, and what to do, so a blank screen never reads as failure.

nodes.label: The Five Copy Rules (Clear, Concise, Consistent, Useful, Human)
nodes.norm_label: the five copy rules (clear, concise, consistent, useful, human)

nodes.label: UX Copy Voice — Calm, Direct, Human
nodes.rationale: Written to read like a wise colleague, never motivational and never clinical, because cheerleading copy makes an overwhelmed practitioner feel the tool is demanding something from them.
nodes.norm_label: ux copy voice — calm, direct, human

nodes.label: Discomfort -> Observation -> Data -> Clarity Sequence
nodes.rationale: Exists to interrupt the pattern of making a permanent decision from a temporary emotion — the evidence log supplies the data step that a practitioner running on feelings would skip.

nodes.label: Evidence Over Vibes
nodes.rationale: did_it is strictly boolean and never nullable because scales reintroduce self-assessment (vibes), binary forces the task definition to be clear, and evidence must be countable — '5 of 7' is a number, 'mostly 3-4 out of 5' is noise.

nodes.label: Pattern Insight Rules
nodes.rationale: Never fire below 14 days of logs and return nothing instead — a fake insight from thin data would be exactly the vibes-based coaching the doctrine exists to prevent. One insight at a time, never stacked.

nodes.label: Consent Before Extraction
nodes.rationale: Always ask before taking; Claude never acts without human confirmation, which is why ai_suggestions.confirmed defaults to false at the database level.

nodes.label: Trip Wire System
nodes.rationale: Resistance is routed to an intervention type (somatic / identity / relational / logistical / clarity / consent) rather than answered with more pressure, because pushing harder on the wrong resistance type is what breaks practitioners.

nodes.label: Review Gate
nodes.rationale: Claude Code stops after every stage output and waits for explicit confirmation; the gate is described as 'not optional, it is the architecture' — auto-proceeding would collapse the human-in-the-loop property ICM is built for.

nodes.label: Paid Tier Gate Pattern
nodes.rationale: AI features render only when practitioner.tier === 'paid' and the gate is clean with no teaser — a locked upsell card would violate the One-Room Rule.

nodes.label: api/claude.ts Vercel Serverless Proxy
nodes.rationale: Exists solely to keep the Anthropic key server-side; max_tokens 300 and temperature 0.3 because suggestions are short by design and consistency beats creativity here.

nodes.label: Claude AI Layer
nodes.rationale: Claude suggests but never acts; every suggestion is persisted and requires human confirmation so the tool cannot coach a practitioner without a human in the loop.

nodes.label: BWYH (Build While You Heal)
nodes.rationale: The ascension path above STB; the Command Center is the stabilization layer beneath it, kept connected but distinct so clients are not sold the deeper program before they are stable.

nodes.label: Supabase (PostgreSQL + Magic Link Auth)
nodes.rationale: Magic link with no password chosen so a half-awake practitioner at 7am never hits a password wall.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Practitioner Shell
nodes.rationale: Stages 01-05 must ship to a real practitioner before the operator view starts, so product-practitioner fit is proven before cohort tooling is paid for.

nodes.label: Stage Map (Stages 01-07)
nodes.rationale: Folder numbering encodes execution order — the stage map is the routing table, not a schedule; a stage is blocked until its predecessor's output is approved.

nodes.label: STB Command Center Tech Stack
nodes.rationale: React 18 + TypeScript + Vite chosen so the app installs on a phone as a PWA with no app store; no server beyond a single Vercel serverless proxy.

nodes.label: React PWA Shell
nodes.rationale: Built as an empty skeleton with placeholder screens on purpose so Stage 03 and 04 only fill in screens and never renegotiate routing or auth.

nodes.label: Agent-Reach Signal Intelligence
nodes.rationale: Chosen for zero API fees across Twitter/Reddit/YouTube; output lands in _config/signals/ as Layer 3 reference so it is loaded as a constraint, not as per-run input.

nodes.label: Graphify Knowledge Graph Integration
nodes.rationale: Rebuilt after each stage so later stages query the graph instead of re-reading full doctrine files, keeping the context window small — the same 'prevention not compression' argument ICM makes.

nodes.label: AI-PROMPT-TEMPLATES.md
nodes.rationale: Prompt templates are written into _config/doctrine/ (Layer 3) rather than embedded in code so they are internalized as stable constraints and are editable without a redeploy.

nodes.label: Context Engineering
nodes.rationale: Karpathy's 2025 framing plus Lance Martin's write/select/compress/isolate taxonomy: prompt engineering understates the work, which is filling the context window with the right instructions, knowledge, memory and prior outputs.

nodes.label: Long-Context Degradation (Liu et al.)
nodes.rationale: LLMs perform significantly worse when relevant information is buried mid-context; the more irrelevant material present, the worse performance on what matters. This is the empirical basis for stage-scoped loading.

nodes.label: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
nodes.rationale: Distinguished from ICM as complementary, not competing: MCP standardizes how models reach external tools; ICM structures how context is delivered across a multi-stage workflow. An ICM stage may use MCP while its folder scopes the context.

nodes.label: Unix Pipeline and Pipe-and-Filter Lineage
nodes.rationale: McIlroy's rules of modularity, transparency and composition, formalized by Shaw and Garlan as pipe-and-filter, plus Feldman's Make: files are simultaneously the artifacts of work and the coordination mechanism between stages.

nodes.label: Interpretable Context Methodology (ICM)
nodes.rationale: Adopted instead of a multi-agent framework because the build workflow is sequential with human review at each step; folder structure carries the orchestration so no coordination code has to be written or redeployed.

nodes.label: Source of Truth Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: An explicit precedence order exists so the agent never has to invent an architectural decision when instructions conflict — it stops and asks instead.

nodes.label: Workspace Routing Rules
nodes.rationale: Layer 1 answers 'where do I go?' — a natural-language request maps to exactly one stage plus the Layer 3 files it may load, so the agent never loads the whole _config directory.

nodes.label: AuthContext
nodes.rationale: Holds session, practitioner profile and tier together because every tier gate in Stages 03-05 reads from one place.

nodes.label: MomentumCard component
nodes.rationale: Deliberately the same component in Today and Evidence so the score can never disagree between screens.

nodes.label: TodayScreen
nodes.rationale: Shows exactly three active items (focus, action, step) plus the momentum card; text debounce-saves at 500ms so nothing needs a save button.

nodes.label: OfferScreen (Offer Clarity)
nodes.rationale: The second doorway is rendered at 60% opacity so it exists without competing with the first doorway for attention.

nodes.label: SprintScreen
nodes.rationale: Max 5 active tasks before 'show more' and completed tasks collapsed by default: the practitioner should see what needs doing, not what is done.

nodes.label: Color Palette Tokens
nodes.rationale: Dark green ground (#0d1f17) with gold (#c9a84c) as the only primary-action accent — depth comes from color layering rather than shadow, giving a cinematic rather than productivity-app feel.

nodes.label: Leak Zone Color Map (6 zones)
nodes.rationale: Hard-coded per zone rather than generated, so the same zone reads the same color on the Sprint board, the Offer screen and the operator view.

nodes.label: daily_entries table
nodes.rationale: UNIQUE (practitioner_id, date) enforces exactly one focus per day — the One-Room Rule expressed as a database constraint.

nodes.label: offers table
nodes.rationale: is_first_doorway is made mutually exclusive with a partial unique index WHERE is_first_doorway = true, so 'one first doorway' is enforced by the database instead of by UI discipline.

nodes.label: practitioners table
nodes.rationale: Carries the three onboarding answers (one_sentence, bleed_zone, stability_goal) directly on the row so the AI layer can build a prompt from a single fetch.

nodes.label: First Doorway
nodes.rationale: Exactly one offer per practitioner is the first doorway; the constraint forces a decision rather than letting a practitioner keep several half-offers alive.

nodes.label: Six Leak Zones
nodes.rationale: offer_clarity, operations, visibility, pricing, delivery, mindset — a fixed taxonomy so tasks, offers and colors all key off the same six values.

nodes.label: Rules That Cannot Be Broken
nodes.rationale: No shadows, no gradients, max 3 items on Today, gold fills only the single primary action per screen, no emoji: each rule removes a way the interface could start competing for attention.

nodes.label: Error Message Structure (What happened -> what to do)
nodes.rationale: Never apologise and never be vague — an apology adds a second emotional beat to a moment where the practitioner only needs the next step.
nodes.norm_label: error message structure (what happened -> what to do)

nodes.label: One-Room Rule
nodes.rationale: Backend complexity is allowed, client-facing complexity is not. Max 3 items above the fold on Today, max 5 active sprint tasks, one AI pill per screen — this prevents task-list anxiety and decision paralysis at the top of the day.

nodes.label: The Operator Exception
nodes.rationale: The One-Room Rule deliberately does not apply to Stage 06 — the operator wants to see the whole cohort, so a different room for a different person with different needs is correct, not a violation.

nodes.label: The 7am Test Question
nodes.rationale: Before shipping a screen change: would a half-awake practitioner at 7am know immediately what to do? If the answer is 'maybe', simplify until it is yes.

nodes.label: offers_leak_zones_valid
nodes.rationale: Constrains the offers leak_zones array to the same six zones as sprint_tasks.leak_zone so the Sprint and Offer screens cannot drift apart.

nodes.label: practitioners_tier Index
nodes.rationale: The Stage 06 operator roster sorts by tier; cheap now, saves a migration later.

nodes.label: practitioners_self_insert Policy
nodes.rationale: No practitioner row is created automatically on sign-up; this policy lets Stage 02 insert exactly one row after first sign-in and nothing more. An on_auth_user_created trigger was left out because the contract does not specify one and onboarding copy belongs to Stage 02.

nodes.label: seed.sql
nodes.rationale: Idempotent; resolves the practitioner by email against auth.users so a missing magic-link sign-in exits with a readable message instead of a foreign key error.

nodes.label: ai_suggestions_never_born_confirmed Trigger
nodes.rationale: A default is only a default and any caller can override it in the INSERT, so the trigger forces confirmed := false on every insert; consent can only be granted by a later human UPDATE.

nodes.label: Generated database.types.ts
nodes.rationale: Types are generated rather than hand-written so they cannot drift from the schema.

nodes.label: service_role BYPASSRLS
nodes.rationale: service_role bypasses RLS entirely so no policy is needed; SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY must never appear in a VITE_-prefixed variable.

nodes.label: Tier Gate On practitioners.tier
nodes.rationale: practitioners.tier is the single source for 'paid' feature gating in Stages 03-05.

nodes.label: Consent Before Extraction
nodes.rationale: Claude never acts without human confirmation; consent must be granted by a later human update, never manufactured by the code that writes the row.

nodes.label: Correction: Remove ai_suggestions_service_insert
nodes.rationale: The policy is deleted outright; Stage 05's serverless function writes suggestions with SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY and is unaffected because policies are never consulted for service_role.

nodes.label: Correction: is_operator() SECURITY DEFINER Helper
nodes.rationale: A table owner bypasses RLS so the lookup inside is not re-filtered and the recursion never starts; it is evaluated once per statement rather than once per row, removing the repeated subquery from the other five tables, and search_path is pinned so it cannot be hijacked.

nodes.label: Defect: ai_suggestions_service_insert Was An Open Door
nodes.rationale: WITH CHECK (true) was commented as restricted at the application layer via the service role key, but an unqualified policy applies to every role that can INSERT, so any signed-in practitioner could fabricate a 'Claude said so' suggestion under another practitioner_id. service_role never needed the policy because it has BYPASSRLS.
nodes.norm_label: defect: ai_suggestions_service_insert was an open door

nodes.label: Defect: Operator Policy On practitioners Was Unrunnable
nodes.rationale: An inline EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM practitioners ...) inside a policy on practitioners makes Postgres re-apply RLS to the subquery; applied verbatim it fails with 'infinite recursion detected in policy for relation practitioners'.
nodes.norm_label: defect: operator policy on practitioners was unrunnable

nodes.label: RLS Enabled Before Any Policy Exists
nodes.rationale: RLS is turned on for all six tables in 001, before a single policy exists, so between migrations the tables are deny-all rather than briefly open.
nodes.norm_label: rls enabled before any policy exists

nodes.label: did_it boolean NOT NULL
nodes.rationale: A 1-5 scale invites self-assessment, which is how vibes get back in. Binary also forces a clear task definition: if you cannot say whether you did it, the task was vague and that is the real problem.

nodes.label: No DELETE Grant On evidence_logs
nodes.rationale: A logged rep is a fact. The UNIQUE (practitioner_id, date) constraint makes correcting today an update rather than a duplicate, but history cannot be deleted to make a streak look better than it was.

nodes.label: Missing STABILITY-SEEKER-ARCHETYPE Input
nodes.rationale: The contract lists the archetype doctrine as a required Layer 3 input but it is absent; the profile columns one_sentence, bleed_zone and stability_goal were built from the archetype description inside EVIDENCE-OVER-VIBES.md and schema.sql, and may need a follow-up migration.

nodes.label: Nested Repo Directory
nodes.rationale: Everything lives one directory deep in STB-COMMAND-CENTER/STB-COMMAND-CENTER/, while every path in CLAUDE.md, CONTEXT.md and all five stage contracts assumes repo root and Vite plus Vercel build detection look at the root. Worth flattening before Stage 02 scaffolds src/.

nodes.label: Not Yet Applied To A Live Supabase Project
nodes.rationale: Verified only against local PostgreSQL 16 with a stand-in auth schema; auth.uid() and auth.users behave the same there but the dashboard auth settings still need doing by hand.
nodes.norm_label: not yet applied to a live supabase project

nodes.label: Operator Authors The Sprint
nodes.rationale: Practitioners cannot INSERT into sprint_tasks because a practitioner who can add their own tasks can quietly rewrite the sprint into something more comfortable, which is the exact avoidance the sprint exists to interrupt.

nodes.label: Suggestions Never Practitioner-Authored
nodes.rationale: Practitioners cannot INSERT into ai_suggestions; suggestions originate from the Stage 05 serverless function or an operator, which is what lets the UI honestly label a row 'Claude suggested this.'

nodes.label: One-Room Rule
nodes.rationale: The room is small and the path is obvious is presented as the design, not a limitation; the interface stays peaceful while the engine runs beneath it.

nodes.label: First Sentence
nodes.rationale: The compression artifact from which offer, pricing, content and funnel all flow. Test: read it to a stranger - if they say 'oh, you help people like me with X' it works.

nodes.label: Compression (Voice Quality)
nodes.rationale: Every sentence earns its place; the instinct is to say more clearly, not more.

nodes.label: Compression Principle
nodes.rationale: A teacher compresses ten years of thinking into one conversation without making the other person feel small. Practitioners do not lack knowledge; they lack compression.

nodes.label: Layer 3 reference schema.sql
nodes.rationale: Layer 3 source of truth for tables, columns, constraints and indexes; outranks the stage contract's abbreviated column list per the source-of-truth hierarchy in CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: Correction: Gaps-And-Islands Streak Ranking
nodes.rationale: Ranks logs by calendar gaps so only genuinely consecutive days count, and requires the run to reach today or yesterday to be live.

nodes.label: Correction: In-Flight Row Passed To The Trigger
nodes.rationale: calculate_momentum_score takes two optional arguments defaulting to NULL so the BEFORE INSERT trigger can hand it the pending row and the one-argument call in the handoff doc still works; the pending row replaces any stored row for the same date, so re-logging corrects rather than double-counts.
nodes.norm_label: correction: in-flight row passed to the trigger

nodes.label: Correction: Single-Normalisation 70/30 Weighting
nodes.rationale: Computes (hits/7) x 70 + (hits/7) x 30 over a true seven-day window so the weights mean what the contract says; a perfect 14-day record now scores exactly 100 and zero evidence logs returns 0.

nodes.label: Defect: First-Ever Log Scored 0
nodes.rationale: The BEFORE INSERT trigger's row is not yet visible to a query against evidence_logs, so the reference call computed from every log except the one being logged; a first-ever rep scored 0, the worst possible first impression of a screen whose job is to show that reps compound.

nodes.label: Defect: Momentum Score Could Never Reach 100
nodes.rationale: The reference multiplies a count-based score (COUNT(*) * 10) by the 0.7/0.3 weights again, normalising twice, and its 'last 7 days' window spans eight calendar days. A perfect 14-day record scored 94, not 100, so the 70/30 split was not 70/30 of anything reachable.
nodes.norm_label: defect: momentum score could never reach 100

nodes.label: Defect: Streak Ignored The Calendar
nodes.rationale: The reference walks logs newest-first counting consecutive did_it rows without comparing dates, so two hits ten days apart counted as a two-day streak (score 14 with a +4 bonus versus 16 with a correct +2).

nodes.label: Out-of-Voice Word List
nodes.rationale: Banned words are rejected for named reasons: hustle-culture energy (grind, crush it), generic marketing filler (unlock, seamless, game-changer), transformation cliche (journey), and condescension (simply, just).

nodes.label: 14-Point Business Bleed Map
nodes.rationale: Expanded from 12 points because you can patch every hole in the bucket and still lose the water if the person carrying it collapses. The 12-point map diagnosed the business entity; the 14-point map also diagnoses the systemic health of the host carrying it.

nodes.label: Pillar 4: Founder Health
nodes.rationale: Added in v2.0 because for relationship-driven practitioners the fatal bleeds sit inside the founder, not in the funnel machinery.

nodes.label: Symptom-to-Bleed Routing
nodes.rationale: Routing keys off the practitioner's own quoted symptom sentence so the operator never has to interpret jargon before assigning a sprint.

nodes.label: Client Interface Doctrine
nodes.rationale: Never show the architecture and never say 'agent orchestration' to a practitioner; the interface must be peaceful.

nodes.label: Practitioner-Facing Banned Words List
nodes.source_location: Copy in the STB Command Center
nodes.rationale: Bleed, diagnostic, intervention, prescribe and triage are banned in practitioner-facing copy and replaced with scan, audit, next step, recommend and clarify.

nodes.label: Public Lexicon Translation Layer
nodes.rationale: Clinical urgency language that converts B2B operators triggers a sympathetic fight-or-flight response in somatic practitioners at the digital doorway. A technically peaceful interface is not emotionally peaceful if the words on the button are wrong, so the same operational rigor is wrapped in resonant language.

nodes.label: 30-Day Sandbox (Stage B.5)
nodes.rationale: Inserted between Translate and Package because jumping straight to commercialization felt abrupt and overwhelming for visionary practitioners; it is a bounded experiment with a day-30 evidence checkpoint, not permission to play indefinitely.

nodes.label: AI Offer Architect
nodes.source_location: What This Means for the STB Command Center
nodes.rationale: Applies the translation interrogation automatically, returns a more compressed version of the practitioner's draft, never accepts 'healing' or 'alignment' untranslated, and surfaces the human before the outcome.

nodes.label: Stage A - Extract
nodes.source_location: Stage A - Extract: The Inquiry of Identity
nodes.rationale: Start with beliefs, not biographies - 'What do you believe that most people in your field get entirely wrong?' - because biographies are common and beliefs are rare, and the question forces a position without asking for a pitch.

nodes.label: Stage B - Translate
nodes.rationale: Ambiguous words (healing, alignment, embodiment) are not wrong, they are untranslated: precise to the founder and vague to everyone else. Translation turns a feeling into a business.

nodes.label: Stage C - Package
nodes.rationale: No technical construction - no landing pages, AI agents or automation - until Stages A, B and B.5 are complete; the human methodology must be stable before the machine amplifies it.

nodes.label: Worldview Extraction
nodes.rationale: Most AI implementations fail because they are implemented before the human is understood; extract the worldview and build the shared vocabulary before introducing technology.

nodes.label: NotebookLM Intelligence Synthesis
nodes.rationale: Two NotebookLM deep-dives acted as a red team on the STB framework; the critique was structural and linguistic rather than hostile, producing calibrations rather than overhauls. The core insight: the engine was excellent, the doorway was wrong.

nodes.label: 15-20 Minute Diagnostic Protocol
nodes.rationale: Points 13 and 14 are conditional gates, not mandatory stops - run only when the founder reports a structural puzzle - so adding them does not bloat the scan into a 90-minute therapy session.

nodes.label: Point 13 - Financial Alignment
nodes.rationale: Healers price bespoke, emotionally intensive work at commodity rates, often as a trauma response rather than a business decision. The bleed is in the margin, not the funnel: you can fill every seat and still destroy the founder financially.

nodes.label: Point 14 - Founder Capacity
nodes.rationale: A healer's business IS the healer, so chronic energetic deficit collapses the quality of the work and the business with it, unlike a product that runs whether the founder is rested or not.

nodes.label: Clinical Language Quarantine Rule
nodes.rationale: The doctrine is not to eliminate clinical language but to quarantine it: full clinical vocabulary internally (operator view, doctrine, AI layer), public lexicon externally. The audience should never feel like they are in a hospital waiting room.

nodes.label: Identify My Growth Leak (Public CTA)
nodes.rationale: Chosen over 'Find My Bleed' because it stays operational (leak = systemic loss) and specific while being emotionally safe for a healer to click, shifting posture from defensive to curious.

nodes.label: Invisible Leakage
nodes.rationale: The core wound is not failure but slippage: leads going quiet, content that does not convert, clients who never refer, delivery that consumes growth time. Naming leakage (not failure) keeps the diagnostic non-shaming.

nodes.label: Stability Seeker Vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Onboarding and copy reuse the practitioner's literal phrases ('I feel like I'm always starting over', 'Everything lives in my head') because clinical or corporate phrasing signals the framework does not understand them and closes the door.

nodes.label: Somatic Trip Wire
nodes.rationale: The nervous system has vetoed the task as outside the window of tolerance; address the state not the task, because urgency and accountability pressure deepen shutdown.

nodes.label: AI Last, Human First
nodes.rationale: AI is the finish line, never the starting line. Generic prompts produce robotic output; worldview-informed prompts produce bespoke output.

nodes.label: Intelligence Quality Axiom
nodes.rationale: The quality of AI output is directly tied to the clarity of extraction. The technology does not get smarter - the human gets clearer and the AI reflects that clarity back as precision. A competitor can copy the tools but not the compressed worldview.

nodes.label: Invisible Water
nodes.rationale: Founders cannot describe their own perspective because it is omnipresent, like water to a fish; the framework acts as a laboratory that creates structured distance so they can observe their own methodology from outside.

nodes.label: Check-In Draft Format
nodes.rationale: Open with an observation not a question, one acknowledgement, one observation, one question OR one suggestion, max four sentences. If it cannot be said in four sentences it needs a call, not a message.

nodes.label: Machine-Readable Evidence Layer
nodes.rationale: The ICU vital signs monitor for a business - it proves the fix is working without requiring the founder to play doctor every day.

nodes.label: 30-Day Continuity Protocol
nodes.rationale: Five phases - Diagnose, Lower the Load, Build First Doorway, Create Evidence, Continue - confirmed as the right post-sprint structure.

nodes.label: Evidence Over Vibes
nodes.source_location: Application to the STB Command Center
nodes.rationale: Binary proof — did the thing or didn't — replaces the emotional weather that otherwise governs the Stability Seeker's sense of momentum.

nodes.label: Trip Wire Protocol
nodes.rationale: Detect, name without labelling, listen for the type, apply the type-specific response, shrink the next action, log it. A resolved trip wire is evidence the system works, not evidence of failure.

nodes.label: Trip Wire System
nodes.rationale: A trip wire is a stall whose cause is not obvious. The most dangerous operator error is prescribing the wrong response to the right signal, so correct type identification always precedes intervention.

nodes.label: Anti-Sand Trap Rule
nodes.rationale: If there is no evidence at day 30 - no conversations, no reactions, no documentation - the sandbox has become avoidance and must be routed to the Trip Wire Detector as a clarity block.

nodes.label: AI Suggestion Confirm/Dismiss Pattern
nodes.source_location: Application to the STB Command Center
nodes.rationale: AI output is framed as a thinking partner ('Claude suggests:') with confirm/dismiss so the practitioner always makes the final call; the system never acts without their consent.

nodes.label: Clarity Trip Wire
nodes.rationale: Action stalls at the decision point; clarity blocks resolve by narrowing, never by adding options or research, which produces more paralysis.

nodes.label: Consent Trip Wire
nodes.rationale: Agreement to the direction was incomplete; anything built on incomplete consent must eventually be rebuilt, so stopping to check consent explicitly saves time later.

nodes.label: Identity Trip Wire
nodes.rationale: The task bumped a belief about who they are allowed to be; anchor to concrete evidence rather than resolving the identity question, because big-picture visioning deepens the spiral.

nodes.label: Logistical Trip Wire
nodes.rationale: A real solvable obstacle, most frequently misdiagnosed as something deeper; over-psychologising it wastes time and makes the practitioner feel more fragile than they are.

nodes.label: Relational Trip Wire
nodes.rationale: The work is done but never sent because of an anticipated reaction; name the relationship, not the task. 'Just send it' erodes trust since they already know they could.

nodes.label: Smallest Possible Action
nodes.rationale: Make the next step smaller than it seems it needs to be; the goal of a trip wire response is to restore motion, not to make up lost time.

nodes.label: Evidence Over Vibes
nodes.rationale: Binary proof only, no partial credit; evidence must not be editable after the fact or the doctrine stops working.

nodes.label: Momentum Score Snapshot Column
nodes.rationale: The momentum_score column on evidence_logs is a snapshot of momentum at log time. Older rows are deliberately never rewritten because the history of the score is itself evidence; Stage 03 calls the function for the live number and reads the column only for charting.

nodes.label: Major Dream Brand Voice
nodes.rationale: Direct, warm, sovereign. Warmth is embedded in the willingness to be direct rather than added as a tone layer, and enthusiasm comes from precision rather than volume.

nodes.label: Precision Over Performance
nodes.rationale: The voice is not trying to impress but to be understood, so filler enthusiasm and exclamation marks as energy substitutes are banned.

nodes.label: Sovereign Authority
nodes.rationale: The voice states what it knows and demonstrates rather than convincing; hedging and permission-seeking break it.

nodes.label: Warmth Without Softness
nodes.rationale: Care shows up as being clear enough that the person knows what to do next; softening dilutes clarity.

nodes.label: Something Hit a Wall Button
nodes.rationale: The practitioner is never asked to self-diagnose a type; they answer one sentence about what stopped. Claude identifies the type internally, the operator confirms, and the practitioner receives only the response, never the diagnosis.
